author: b8e438631b034d8e
text: For a producer, the first question isn't which machine. It's what the electricity will cost, and for how long. Get that number low and every machine you ever plug in makes its bitcoin for less than the next miner's does.

author: b8e438631b034d8e
text: Our mining-vs-buying study: 261 machine purchases, every month from 2018 to 2022, each against the same dollars put straight into bitcoin. Share that ended with more bitcoin than buying: 3¢ power: 87% 4.5¢: 57% 5¢: 48% 6.5¢: 35%

author: b8e438631b034d8e
text: What nobody can buy off the shelf is someone else's power price. A machine pays its rate on every kilowatt-hour, every day, for years. A cent or two looks small on a contract. Over a machine's life it decides who ends up with more bitcoin.

author: b8e438631b034d8e
text: Same twelve mining machines. Same purchase months, 2018 to 2022. Same bitcoin price, every power bill paid. On 3¢ power, 87% of those purchases ended with more bitcoin than buying. On 6.5¢, 35%. The machines didn't change. Only the electricity did.
